# Gradle build script counters (build.gradle and settings.gradle in the Groovy DSL, build.gradle.kts
# and settings.gradle.kts in the Kotlin DSL), for a rule with the prompt file-body-ops: one per line,
# label TAB pattern (Java regex). The [ignore] line blanks, leftmost region first, line and block
# comments and string literals (Groovy's single, double and triple quotes, Kotlin's raw strings), so
# a commented-out dependency does not count; a comment or a triple-quoted string that is never closed
# runs to the end of the file, a quoted string to the end of its line. A declaration counts by its keyword at the start of a line, not an
# assignment or a property of that name (implementation.extendsFrom, id = ...). "plugins" counts
# id, alias, kotlin(...), a backquoted plugin id, a core plugin the Kotlin DSL names bare (java,
# application, jacoco, ...; not the java { } block) and apply plugin, at the start of a line or
# after a { or ; (plugins { java; id("x") } is two), not an id next to a name, email, url,
# implementationClass or another key of a developer or a plugin declaration on its line or the line
# before or after it (pom { developers { developer { id 'jdoe' } } }, gradlePlugin { plugins { x {
# id 'org.x' } } }); "repositories" a repository, not a publication (maven(MavenPublication));
# "tasks registered, created or configured" a tasks.register, create, named, withType or getByName,
# a Kotlin accessor block (tasks.test { }) and Groovy's task name, not a task an argument list or a
# dependsOn, finalizedBy, mustRunAfter or shouldRunAfter refers to; "dependency declarations" a
# dependency in one of the standard configurations of the java, kotlin and annotation-processor
# plugins, at the start of a line or after a { or ;; "project dependencies" project(...) and Kotlin's projects.name accessors; "include and
# includeBuild statements" the statements, not the projects one names (include("core", "web") is one):
# include at the start of a line, as settings.gradle writes it (an indented include is a copy spec's
# or a test task's pattern), includeBuild indented too (pluginManagement { includeBuild(...) }).
# OpsFactPatternsTest pins every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every pattern
# reads linearly.
[ignore] comments and string literals
plugins
dependency declarations
project dependencies
platforms and BOMs
repositories
tasks registered, created or configured
include and includeBuild statements
version catalog references
